items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It’d be fitting in a Woody Allen movie.

ctx.x: It’s, it’s ironic and funny, that’s… I was playing at Sweet Basil years ago, and I think it was a Saturday night. It was really crowded. I was working with Brookmeyer, just the two of us. So I went in the kitchen and I got a cup of coffee, and I was standing outside the club on Bleeker Street. And there was a lot of traffic. It was a busy evening and I was just kinda thinking. And I felt this arm around my neck, really strong, and I thought it was a friend putting me on or something. Then I noticed whoever it was…
That’s a New York moment. It’d be fitting in a Woody Allen movie.
